title: Telemetry Contract Evolution and Backwards-Compatibility Playbook
author: Aria Nelson
body:
Overview
=========
This playbook describes a standardized process for evolving telemetry contracts (event/metric/log schemas, labels/tags, sampling, and retention metadata) while preserving backwards compatibility for dashboard owners, alerting rules, downstream consumers, and cost-sensitive exporters. It targets platform teams, instrumentation owners, and operators responsible for telemetry producers and consumers.

Goals
-----
- Minimize user-facing breakages when telemetry changes are required.
- Provide deterministic validation and rollout paths for schema and sampling changes.
- Ensure cost and retention impacts are quantified and approved before rollout.
- Give dashboard/alert owners a clear migration window and testing harness.

Scope
-----
Applies to: structured telemetry events (JSON), metric time series, tracing spans, and log enrichment fields emitted by platform services, sidecars, and agent collectors.
Does not apply to: ad-hoc internal debugging logs emitted to ephemeral channels or node-local debug sinks.

Key Concepts and Definitions
----------------------------
- Producer: service or library that emits telemetry (e.g., runtime, gateway, worker).
- Consumer: dashboards, alert rules, billing pipelines, external integrations.
- Contract: the formal schema (fields, types, units, tags) and semantic guarantees for an event/metric/span.
- Schema Version: a semantic version (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH) used for telemetry contracts.
- Compatibility: producers and consumers can agree on compatibility rules (additive changes, optional fields, stable tag names).

Versioning Rules (summary)
-------------------------
- MAJOR: incompatible semantic changes (rename/remove required fields, change units). Requires explicit cross-team sign-off and 60-day migration window.
- MINOR: additive, backward-compatible additions (new optional fields, new metrics). Requires 14-day consumer notice and automated CI validation.
- PATCH: non-semantic fixes (typos in docs, non-consumer-visible renames in metadata). No broadcast required but must be documented.

Contract Authoring Checklist
---------------------------
1) Identify the producer and single-point owner.
2) Draft the contract change in the telemetry spec repo (see examples below).
3) Classify change as MAJOR/MINOR/PATCH. Justify classification.
4) Add migration notes, expected cardinality and cost delta (tokens/GB/day).
5) Add automated contract tests (see CI section).
6) Create a migration issue and tag affected consumer teams.

Example: JSON event contract (minor)
----------------------------------
```json
{
  "schema_version": "1.2.0",
  "event_type": "model_inference.request",
  "fields": {
    "request_id": {"type": "string", "required": true},
    "model": {"type": "string", "required": true},
    "latency_ms": {"type": "number", "required": false},
    "client_tier": {"type": "string", "required": false, "enum": ["self-serve","enterprise"]}
  }
}
```

Compatibility rules demonstrated:
- Adding client_tier is MINOR because it is optional.
- Removing request_id would be MAJOR (not allowed without migration).

CI Validation and Contract Tests
--------------------------------
Every change proposal must add or update tests in the telemetry-specs CI job. The CI job runs three checks:
1) Schema lint (jsonschema validation).
2) Consumer regression harness: replay a sample of production messages through consumer mocks to detect missing fields or type mismatches.
3) Cardinality/cost estimate sanity check: compares expected cardinality annotations to historical counts and flags >20% delta without justification.

Sample CI config snippet (telemetry-specs/.github/workflows/validate-telemetry.yml)
```yaml
name: Validate Telemetry
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  validate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Run schema lint
        run: telemetry-lint ./specs
      - name: Run consumer replay tests
        run: telemetry-replay --sample ./specs/samples
      - name: Cardinality check
        run: telemetry-cardinality-check --baseline last-30d
```

Dashboard and Alert Owner Workflow
----------------------------------
1) Notification: For MINOR/PATCH changes, the telemetry owner must post an RFC to #telemetry-updates Slack and add an entry to the telemetry migration board. For MAJOR changes, open a migration RFC and schedule a migration sync.
2) Consumer mapping: maintain a table mapping consumers to dashboards/alerts and ownership. Example table (text table):

| Consumer | Dashboard / Alert | Owner | Sensitivity |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| inference-metrics | model-latency-99th | @ml-observability | high |
| routing-service | edge-error-rate | @infra-observability | medium |

3) Staging validation: Deploy the producer change behind a feature flag in staging and run end-to-end replay into a shadow consumer cluster.
4) Canary: Enable the new schema production-side in canary region with 5–10% traffic. Confirm no alert firing and dashboards render.
5) Gradual rollout: 25% -> 50% -> 100% with 24–48h observation windows.
6) Deprecation: After migration window expires, schedule MAJOR removals and document migration success.

Rollout Safety Gates
--------------------
- Unit tests: pass all contract unit checks.
- No regression alerts: no new fires in canary window.
- Cost delta approval: finance or platform budget owner signs off if expected daily ingest increases >10%.
- Post-deploy smoke: synthetic queries for affected dashboards must return within 2x baseline latency.

Emergency rollback steps
------------------------
1) If alerts indicate consumer breakage, flip producer feature flag off.
2) If producer-side flag cannot be toggled, deploy a compatibility shim in the collector (transform new payloads to old shape).
3) Open an incident and run the telemetry contract rollback runbook (link).
4) Postmortem required for any production brokenness > 10 minutes.

Collector and Exporter Transform Patterns
----------------------------------------
When consumer upgrades lag, use the collector to present a compatibility layer:
- Field aliasing: map new_field -> old_field when present.
- Default injection: if new boolean field omitted, inject default value for consumers.
- Backfill enrichment: on ingestion, enrich events with derived tags to satisfy old alert rules.
Example transform (pseudoyaml):
```yaml
transform:
  - when: has("client_tier")
    map: {"old_tier": "client_tier"}
  - when: not has("latency_ms")
    inject: {"latency_ms": 0}
```

Cost and Retention Considerations
--------------------------------
Before approving schema changes, instrumentation owners must provide:
- Estimated per-event size (bytes) and change in daily GB.
- Expected increase in timeseries cardinality (new tag cardinality).
- Retention impact: which signals need longer retention and justification.
- Owner signs off: @platform-billing or finance as required.

Migration Timeline Examples
--------------------------
- Minor (e.g., optional field): 14-day notice on board, staged canary, 7–14 day observation, close ticket.
- Major (e.g., rename required field): 60-day migration window, compatibility shim mandatory, weekly migration status updates, final removal scheduled at end of window.

Observability and Dashboard Tests (Checklist)
--------------------------------------------
- Dashboard render test: automated screenshot test in staging and canary.
- Alert runbook verification: verify runbook links and escalation points remain accurate after schema change.
- Query resilience: replace strict field references with existence checks where appropriate.

Migration Example: model_id rename -> model_name (MAJOR)
----------------------------------------------------
1) Publish RFC describing reason and migration steps.
2) Add producer to emit both model_id and model_name for 60 days (dual-write).
3) Update dashboards to prefer model_name but fall back to model_id.
4) Run consumer replay tests and invite dashboard owners to validate rendered results.
5) After 60 days and zero blockers, remove model_id in a coordinated MAJOR change.

Post-change Retrospective and Metrics to Track
----------------------------------------------
- Number of dashboards that required manual updates.
- Incidents or alert noise attributable to the change.
- Observed versus predicted cost delta.
- Time to full consumer migration.

Retrospective template (to be filled after migration)
- Summary: short description of change.
- What worked: list successes.
- What failed: where rollback or shims were needed.
- Action items: concrete follow-ups with owners and due dates.

Ownership and Contacts
----------------------
- Telemetry producer owner: single person/team listed on the spec.
- Telemetry platform steward: @platform-telemetry (triage and CI).
- Finance cost approver: @platform-billing.
- Oncall escalation: see team oncall roster (link).

Appendices
---------
A) Quick reference: compatibility rules (one-liner):
- Add fields -> safe (MINOR).
- Change semantics/units -> MAJOR.
- Rename/remove required fields -> MAJOR and needs shim.

B) Quick CLI: locally validate a sample file against spec
```bash
pipx run telemetry-lint specs/model_inference.json && telemetry-replay --sample samples/model_inference_sample.json
```

C) Example consumer fallback SQL snippet for dashboards
```sql
-- prefer new tag, fallback to old
SELECT
  coalesce(event.tags->>'model_name', event.tags->>'model_id') as model_label,
  p50(latency_ms) as p50
FROM telemetry_events
WHERE event_type = 'model_inference.request'
GROUP BY model_label
```

D) Links and references:
- telemetry-specs repo: git+ssh://git.company/internal/telemetry-specs
- Collector transform docs: /confluence/eng-platform/systems-and-services/collector-transform-reference
